source.title: Some open problems and research directions in the mathematical study of fluid dynamics.

accepted.question_text: For the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations without external energy input, what are the most general assumptions on a smooth initial velocity field u(x,0) that guarantee the corresponding solution exists for all positive time and remains smooth for all positive time?

evidence.quote: What are the most general conditions for smooth incompressible velocities u(x, 0) that ensure, in the absence of external input of energy, that the solutions of the Navier-Stokes equations exist for all positive time and are smooth?

accepted.question_text: Given an arbitrary infinitely differentiable, divergence-free, compactly supported initial velocity field on ℝ^3 for the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations, must the resulting solution remain smooth for all time?
accepted.context_brief: Compactly supported smooth data in ℝ^3

evidence.quote: A specific regularity question, still open, is for instance: Given an arbitrary infinitely differentiable, incompressible, compactly supported initial velocity field in R3, does the solution remain smooth for all time?

accepted.question_text: Given an arbitrary three-dimensional divergence-free periodic real analytic initial velocity field for the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations, must the resulting solution remain smooth for all time?

evidence.quote: A version of the same question is: Given an arbitrary three-dimensional divergence-free periodic real analytic initial velocity, does the ensuing solution remain smooth for all time?

accepted.question_text: When one modifies the Navier–Stokes equations to force regularity by adding higher-order dissipation, filtering the velocity, adding nonlinear regularizing terms, or projecting to a finite-dimensional energy-preserving system, which modification is the mathematically and physically appropriate one, and does the choice of regularizing modification matter for describing macroscopic fluid behavior?

evidence.quote: There are many ways one may choose to modify the model so that one has regularity. One can add a bi-Laplacian (or some other elliptic operator of high enough order). Or, one can filter the velocity. Or, one can add non-linear regularizing terms. Or, one can project the whole equation on some finite dimensional space, respecting the energy balance. Which modification should one choose? Does it matter?

accepted.question_text: For three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes flow, can one bridge the gap between the vorticity control currently known for general solutions—namely square-integrability of vorticity in space-time together with the averaged geometric bound ν∫∫|ω(x,t)||∇ξ(x,t)|² dx dt < ∞ for the vorticity direction field ξ = ω/|ω|—and the substantially stronger conditions such as ω ∈ L⁴(dt;L²(dx)) or essentially Lipschitz control of ξ in high-vorticity regions that are known to imply smoothness?

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, the only information generally available is ω ∈ L2(dt; L2(dx)). There is a finite gap between what is known and what needs to be known.
This is another example of the gap between what is known to be true and what is needed to be known for regularity.

accepted.question_text: For the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations with smooth finite-energy initial data, do smooth solutions persist for all time, or can a singularity form in finite time?

evidence.quote: So, the question is: Do smooth solutions of Euler equations persist for all time?

accepted.question_text: For the time-independent forced two-dimensional spatially periodic Navier–Stokes equations, can the dynamics on the global attractor be shown to be conjugate to those of a finite-dimensional smooth dynamical system, with the remaining infinitely many degrees of freedom behaving as transient modes in a quantitatively controllable way—in other words, does an inertial-manifold-type finite-dimensional parameterization capturing the full long-time dynamics exist?

evidence.quote: Can one truly say that the dynamics on the attractor are conjugate to the dynamics of a finite dimensional smooth dynamical system and that the rest of the infinitely many degrees of freedom are transient in a controllable fashion? This is the question of inertial manifolds, as open now as it was when it was born ([18]), in the eighties.

accepted.question_text: Can one build a mathematically satisfactory turbulence theory for measures on function space that are supported on Navier–Stokes solution paths, including rigorous results on whether such measures exist and whether they are time-independent or time-dependent, unique or non-unique, symmetric or symmetry-breaking, stable or unstable under perturbations, and how they bifurcate or depend on physical parameters?

evidence.quote: The existence of measures in function space that are supported on Navier-Stokes solution paths, their time-independence or dependence, their uniqueness or lack thereof, their symmetries or lack thereof, their dependence on parameters, their stability, bifurcations and so on..., are the subject of a mathematical turbulence theory.

accepted.question_text: For steady far-field flow past a bounded simply connected obstacle B in the exterior domain Ω = ℝ^3 \ B, with velocity approaching a nonzero constant vector U at spatial infinity, what realistic rigorous upper bounds can be proved for the rate of energy dissipation?

evidence.quote: A specific open problem remains: to provide realistic upper bounds for the dissipation in flow past an obstacle. (Ω = R3 \B, B a bounded simply connected set, u → U 6= 0 as x → ∞.)

accepted.question_text: For classical boundary-driven Navier–Stokes turbulence, can one obtain rigorous estimates and a satisfactory mathematical analysis for higher-order statistical observables such as the velocity moments Um(y,s), the structure functions ⟨|u(x+y,t)-u(x,t)|^m⟩, and the analogous moments and structure functions of the Eulerian–Lagrangian back-to-labels map A(x,t)?
accepted.context_brief: Rigorous bounds for turbulence structure statistics

evidence.quote: The next level of questions concerns averages of functions rather than averages of numbers. Traditional examples are the energy spectrum ([30]), moments ... and, in particular ... structure functions h|u(x + y, t) − u(x, t)|m i.

The Eulerian-Lagrangian approach ([31]) allows one to formulate questions regarding moments of the “back-to-labels ” map ... One can prove some rigorous bounds for norms of such objects and their derivatives in the spatially periodic case. But much remains to be done in the classical, boundary driven Navier-Stokes turbulence problems.
